source_text: Analogies to female genital mutilation (FGM) underscore this, positing both as culturally driven cuttings infringing bodily inviolability, though bioethicists critique the comparison for overlooking graded differences in severity, intent, and outcomes—FGM typically lacks any argued preventive rationale, rendering the ethical symmetry incomplete without equivalent evidence of net utility. [52]
